title: Realization of an etale sheaf over an algebraic-space base
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme and $H$ an algebraic space over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the universes and small skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention], the small etale scheme site of $H$, and sheaves of sets on it [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use chartwise etale maps of algebraic spaces [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], with no representability requirement on their structure maps to $H$, and the canonical inverse images of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. For a sheaf $F$, define the functor on $B$-schemes
$$E_H(F)(T)=\{(h,s)\mid h:T\to H,\ s\in\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},h^{-1}F)\},$$
with restriction along $g:T'\to T$ sending $(h,s)$ to $(hg,g^{-1}s)$, using the canonical composition comparison. Impose the following explicit size convention: the ambient scheme site contains the coproduct of the scheme generators with sections used to present each sheaf under consideration; equivalently one may enlarge the ambient universe before making the construction. Then $E_H(F)$ is an algebraic space, the map $E_H(F)\to H$ is chartwise etale, and the functor
$$V\longmapsto h_V,\qquad h_V(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_H(U,V),$$
from chartwise etale algebraic spaces over $H$ to sheaves on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an equivalence, with quasi-inverse $E_H$. Here the spaces and sheaves are taken in the common bound just specified. The unit $F\simeq h_{E_H(F)}$ and counit $E_H(h_V)\simeq V$ are natural in all sheaf maps and all $H$-morphisms of spaces. This statement does not assume that $H$ is a scheme or that $V\to H$ is representable, separated, quasi-compact or finite.

source.place: Tag 0GF6 (lemma-sheaf-gives-space), construction preceding the lemma, parts (1)-(3), and its size condition; full faithfulness is the natural counit of that construction.

proof.text: Use the common size bound in the statement and [def-weil-size-convention]. Schemes are fppf sheaves by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. More generally, for every algebraic space $A$ over $B$, the presheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_H(U,A)$ on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a sheaf: a small etale covering is an fppf covering by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-pc-fppf-site]; the fppf sheaf axiom for $A$ glues the maps, and their composites to $H$ agree with the structure map because $H$ is an fppf sheaf. Thus representables of scheme objects, and all the displayed $h_A$, are sheaves. We may compute their fibre products sectionwise.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, representable sheaves and the two sheaf categories used in the presentation.

proof.text: For each pair $(U,a)$ with $U$ in the small skeleton of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $a\in F(U)$, take one copy of $U$. This is a set of pairs. Form its scheme coproduct $P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], allowed by the explicit size hypothesis. The summand maps to $H$ glue using the fppf sheaf axiom for $H$. For every scheme $T\to H$, $T\times_HP$ is a scheme by the representable diagonal of $H$. Its open summands $T\times_HU$ cover it and are etale over $T$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] makes $T\times_HP\to T$ etale. Thus $P\to H$ is representable etale. The sections $a$ glue on the disjoint summands to $a_P\in F(P)$. Yoneda gives $p:h_P\to F$. Every $a\in F(U)$ is the image of its summand inclusion $U\to P$; hence $p$ is surjective on sections and is an epimorphism: two maps agreeing after $p$ agree on every section.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, representable generators and the set-theoretic condition; Tag 00WS, lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Put $W=P\times_HP$, a scheme since $H$ has representable diagonal. It is etale over $H$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. On $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ consider the presheaf with one element on $Z\to W$ exactly when the two restrictions of $a_P$ agree, and empty otherwise. It is a subsheaf of the final sheaf: equality is preserved by restriction and can be checked on covers. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-subsheaf-final-open] it is represented by an open subscheme $R\subset W$. Every $H$-map $Z\to W$ between scheme objects of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ is etale by the same permanence node, so the representing property applies to every pair of maps $b,c:Z\to P$ over $H$. It says precisely $(b,c)$ factors through $R$ if and only if $p(b)=p(c)$. Thus $h_R=h_P\times_Fh_P$ on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, paragraph beginning Observe; the omitted support detail uses Tag 04HV (lemma-support-subsheaf-final).

proof.text: The projections $R\rightrightarrows P$ are etale: $R\subset W$ is open, and $W\rightrightarrows P$ is the base change of the representable etale map $P\to H$. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity of equality in $F$ give maps $P\to R$, $R\to R$ and $R\times_PR\to R$ by the kernel-pair identity of Step 3 and Yoneda. All these domains are scheme objects etale over $H$, by permanence. Their projection identities prove reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity on every $B$-scheme test, not merely on etale tests. The map $R\to P\times_BP$ is a monomorphism: a section is determined by its two projections, since $R\subset P\times_HP$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer] to the epimorphism $p$. It follows that $F$ is the coequalizer of $h_R\rightrightarrows h_P$ on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, etale equivalence relation and first coequalizer diagram; Tag 086K (lemma-coequalizer-surjection).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], the fppf sheaf quotient $Q=P/R$ is an algebraic space over $B$, with representable surjective etale atlas $q:P\to Q$ and kernel pair $R$. The two maps $R\rightrightarrows P\to H$ agree, so the universal property in that node gives $Q\to H$. Its composite with $q$ is the representable etale map $P\to H$. The source-atlas criterion [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection](3) now makes $Q\to H$ chartwise etale. This asserts no representability of $Q\to H$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, quotient construction and parts (1),(2); Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation) and Tag 03FS (lemma-etale-local).

proof.text: For a scheme object $U\to H$ and a map $U\to Q$, $U\times_QP\to U$ is a representable surjective etale scheme map and is a covering in $H_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus every section of $h_Q$ locally lifts to $h_P$. If two sheaf maps out of $h_Q$ agree after $h_P$, apply these lifts and the separatedness axiom of their target to show they agree on every section. Hence $h_P\to h_Q$ is epimorphic. Its sectionwise kernel pair is $h_R$, by the quotient node. The effective-epimorphism coequalizer theorem makes $h_Q$ the coequalizer of the same pair as $F$. The two universal properties yield a unique isomorphism $c:F\xrightarrow{\sim}h_Q$ carrying $p$ to $q$.

source.place: Tag 0GF6(3), matching the two presentations; Tag 086K.

proof.text: On the enlarged site $\mathcal C_H$, every represented presheaf $h_A$ is a sheaf. Here is the descent check needed for the adjunction below. Given a covering $Z_i\to Z$ and compatible maps $Z_i\to A$, choose a scheme atlas $U\to Z$. Choose scheme atlases $U_{ij}\to Z_i\times_ZU$. By chartwise permanence, the maps $U_{ij}\to U$ are etale and jointly surjective; hence they are an fppf covering. The maps $U_{ij}\to A$ agree on overlaps (their composites through the $Z_i$ do), and the fppf sheaf axiom for $A$ glues them to $U\to A$. The two maps on $U\times_ZU$ agree after the covering obtained by pulling back the $U_{ij}$, hence agree by the same axiom. For any scheme $T\to Z$, the map $T\times_ZU\to T$ is a surjective etale scheme map, so the map to $A$ descends uniquely to $T$. These descents commute with every $T'\to T$ by uniqueness and define $Z\to A$ as a morphism of fppf sheaves. They restrict to the specified maps on every $Z_i$, tested on scheme atlases; uniqueness follows by the same test. Scheme-density identifies the restriction of this represented sheaf with the small-site $h_A$.

source.place: Tags 03G0 and 03G1, subcanonical enlarged site and scheme-atlas comparison; elementary fppf descent of maps spelled out.

proof.text:
We will use the following elementary adjunction calculation. Work on the enlarged sites of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Representable presheaves there are sheaves by Step 7. For $h:T\to H$, an etale space $A\to H$ and any sheaf $G$ on the enlarged site of $T$, adjunction and Yoneda give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(h^{-1}h_A,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_A,h_*G)=(h_*G)(A)=G(T\times_HA)=\operatorname{Hom}(h_{T\times_HA},G).$$
Thus $h^{-1}h_A\simeq h_{T\times_HA}$, naturally in $A$, $h$ and $G$. The direct-image evaluation here is precisely precomposition by $A\mapsto T\times_HA$ in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]. Transport across the scheme-restriction equivalences gives the same formula on the small sites. This calculation does not require $A\to H$ representable.

Apply Step 8 directly with $A=Q$ and then apply $h^{-1}$ to $c$ of Step 6. Since $T\times_HQ\to T$ is chartwise etale by permanence, it is an object of the enlarged site of $T$. Its represented sheaf evaluated at the terminal object $T/T$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T,T\times_HQ)$. Consequently
$$\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},h^{-1}F)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_T(T,T\times_HQ)=\operatorname{Hom}_H(T,Q).$$
The first equality of section functors uses the scheme-restriction equivalence, which contains $T/T$. The last bijection sends a section to its $Q$-component and sends $a:T\to Q$ over $H$ to $(1_T,a)$. By the adjunction and Yoneda naturalities in Step 8, pulling a section back along $g:T'\to T$ sends its corresponding map $a$ to $ag$. Taking the disjoint union over $h:T\to H$ therefore gives an isomorphism of the stated presheaf $E_H(F)$ with the underlying fppf sheaf of $Q$, over $H$. This proves its algebraicity and chartwise etaleness.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, construction before the lemma and parts (1)-(3); Tag 03G2 and the representable adjunction calculation.

proof.text:
For completeness, the representable adjunction of Step 8 applies to every chartwise etale algebraic space $V\to H$, with no presentation choice. The presheaf $h_V$ is a sheaf by Step 1. It yields natural bijections
$$\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{et}},h^{-1}h_V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_H(T,V).$$
Their disjoint union over $h:T\to H$ defines the counit $E_H(h_V)\simeq V$. The adjunction bijections commute with postcomposition by every $H$-morphism $V\to V'$ and with restriction by every $T'\to T$; hence the counit is natural in all these morphisms. The fibre-product bijection is again $a\mapsto(1_T,a)$, so it introduces no extra representability condition.

source.place: Tag 0GF6, natural counit of the displayed construction; Tag 03G2.

proof.text: If $u:U\to H$ is a scheme object of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$, its inverse image is restriction to the localized site, by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Therefore $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},u^{-1}F)=F(U)$. On the other hand, from the definition of $E_H(F)$ a map over $H$ from $U$ to this space is exactly a pair with fixed first component $u$, hence exactly such a section. This gives $F(U)\simeq h_{E_H(F)}(U)$. Restriction precomposes the first component and pulls back the second, so these bijections commute with every arrow of $H_{\mathrm{et}}$. They commute with every sheaf map $F\to F'$ because that map acts on the second component by its inverse image. Thus they form the natural unit. The natural unit and counit exhibit the two functors as quasi-inverse equivalences.

source.place: Tag 0GF6(3), localization formula for etale scheme objects; Tag 03LP (lemma-etale-morphism-topoi).

lean.statement: theorem spaceEtaleSheaf_realization (H : AlgebraicSpace B) : ∃ e : SpaceEtaleSheaves H ≌ H.EnlargedEtaleSite, e.inverse = spaceEtaleBoundedHomFunctor H ∧ ∃ b : ∀ (F : SpaceEtaleSheaves H) (T : Over B), (schemeSpace T ⟶ (e.functor.obj F).obj.left) ≃ SpaceRealizationPairs H F.obj T, (∀ (F : SpaceEtaleSheaves H) (T : Over B) (a : schemeSpace T ⟶ (e.functor.obj F).obj.left), (b F T a).1 = a ≫ (e.functor.obj F).obj.hom) ∧ (∀ (F : SpaceEtaleSheaves H) (T T' : Over B) (g : T' ⟶ T) (a : schemeSpace T ⟶ (e.functor.obj F).obj.left), b F T' (spaceRealizationSchemeMap g ≫ a) = spaceRealizationPairRestrict H F.obj g (b F T a)) ∧ (∀ (F G : SpaceEtaleSheaves H) (a : F ⟶ G) (T : Over B) (s : schemeSpace T ⟶ (e.functor.obj F).obj.left), b G T (s ≫ (e.functor.map a).hom.left) = spaceRealizationPairMap H a.hom T (b F T s))
lean.note: The theorem gives an equivalence whose inverse is the actual relative Hom functor, and natural pair-formula bijections on every B-scheme test fixing the projection to H. The common size bound is a scheme presentation (an epi from a scheme Hom sheaf), exactly the coproduct-presentation condition in Stacks 0GF6.
